subject: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — rollout coordination
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — kickoff

Marcus / Evelyn —

Following the product sync this morning, I want to kick off a focused coordination thread for the "Mosaic" console view we discussed: a compact grid that surfaces per-tenant cost + median/tail latency, with quick drilldowns into the top 3 expensive routes and a link to trace playback. The ask is to define the MVP data model, ownership, and a short rollout plan (canary cohorts + alerting thresholds).

Key goals:
- Make the unit economics visible to account managers (cost per 1k tokens and tail latency percentiles)
- Provide a clear signal for automated fallback policy triggers (when tenant latency > X and cost spike > Y)
- Keep the first rollout limited to 10 enterprise tenants to validate instrumentation and UX

I attached a rough wireframe (mosaic-wireframe-v1.png) and a sample tenant CSV so we can map columns.

Questions I want covered in the first pass:
1) What telemetry fields do infra/telemetry need to emit to populate per-route cost + P50/P95/P99 for tenant slices?
2) Who will own the frontend surface and the backend aggregation? Proposed: Marcus (backend aggregation) + Evelyn (frontend UX) + Jordan (product rollout ops).
3) What are pragmatic alert thresholds for canary tenants vs GA?

Please reply with short answers / action items. I want to capture this before EOD so we can add to the roadmap sprint.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mosaic-wireframe-v1.png (image/png, sketch)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — kickoff

Thanks — good framing. Short answers below.

1) Telemetry fields: we need per-request metadata: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, host_gpu_type, and an ingest_time. For cost we emit a per-request token_cost_estimate (microcents) computed at the edge aggregation layer; for latency we capture total_ms and kv_cache_hit boolean.

2) Ownership: happy to take backend aggregation. I suggest a lightweight time-bucketed aggregator (1m buckets) that writes pre-aggregates to the insights DB with tenant+route keys. That keeps the query cost reasonable. We can reuse the existing route-agg lambda (with a new cost plugin).

3) Thresholds: for canary tenants start with P95 > 1200ms or a 5x cost deviation from baseline for 3 consecutive windows (1m buckets aggregated over 15m). GA thresholds can be tightened after 2 weeks of telemetry.

Action items:
- Marcus: prototype aggregator + schema by July 6
- Evelyn: wire up front-end prototype to the wireframe and validate with sample CSV by July 9
- Jordan: pick 8–10 canary tenants (ops + AM input) by July 3

I'll follow up with a short PRD that outlines schema and storage footprint.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-28T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — kickoff

Soojin / Marcus —

Appreciate the heads-up. From Acme's side, two asks: (1) please include a column for 'feature_flag_version' so our engineers can correlate spikes to client toggles, and (2) keep the first canary list limited to accounts on dedicated capacity vs hosted — that will avoid mixing noise from multi-tenant bursts.

If it helps, I'll send over a short CSV of our feature-flag windows next week.

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director of ML Platforms
Acme Corp

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood@redwood.ai>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — kickoff

Love the wireframe — small UX notes and a proposed rollout cadence:

UX notes:
- Top-left: tenant selector with account health pill (green/yellow/red) using P95 and cost delta
- Center: mosaic grid where each cell is a tenant; hover reveals last 24h trend sparkline and 3 highest-cost routes
- Drill: clicking a cell opens a right rail with a quick link to trace playback and to the 'apply fallback' action (requires RBAC check)

Rollout cadence: prototype -> internal dogfood (2 weeks) -> canary customers (3 weeks) -> GA. That maps to a July 30 GA if we hit Marcus/Evelyn deadlines.

Attachments: tenant-sample-cases.csv (I sanitized fields, includes a dedicated_capacity boolean and a feature_flag_version column).

I can take the frontend lead; will pair with UI Eng for accessibility and perf.

Eve
Evelyn Hart
Product Designer, Console UX
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>, CloudPartner Integrations <partner-integrations@cloudpartner.io>
Date: 2028-06-29T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Mosaic view for per-tenant cost & latency — kickoff

All good — short operations notes:

- I'll schedule a 30-minute rollout sync for July 10 with AMs + CS + Infra.
- We should instrument a rollback plan: if canary tenants show >10% error increase or P99 latency regresses, we auto-disable the new aggregation (we need a runbook + one-click rollback toggle in Console).
- Partner ask: I looped CloudPartner to ensure we can surface marketplace metadata in the tenant selector (they confirmed they can provide account marketplace ids).

Next steps: Marcus to open the aggregator repo and label an RFC. Evelyn to drop the prototype link in the Drive doc. Soojin to confirm final canary list by July 3.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Product Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none
